book.name: Epistle to the Alexandrians (proposed fragment)
book.title: Proposed Fragment of the Epistle to the Alexandrians · James 1924
book.sourceNote: Four-paragraph public-domain text printed by M. R. James on scan pages 517–518 and transcribed on Wikisource (oldid 11900160). Editorial introduction and commentary are excluded.
book.identityNote: The Bobbio Sacramentary and Lectionary lesson is headed as Colossians. Zahn proposed that it was a fragment of the Epistle to the Alexandrians; James doubted that it was an apocryphon. It is therefore presented only as an uncertain proposed fragment, not as a recovered continuous Pauline letter.
book.rights: M. R. James's 1924 English text is public domain in the United States. Source transcription retrieved from Wikisource; page contributions are available under CC BY-SA.

1.label: Fragment 1
1.text: Brethren, we that are under the power of the Lord ought to keep the commandment of God. They that keep the Lord’s precepts have eternal life, and they that deny his commandments get to themselves ruin and thereto the second death. Now the precept of the Lord is this: Thou shalt not swear falsely, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not bear false witness, thou shalt not take gifts against the truth, neither for power.

1.label: Fragment 2
1.text: Whoso hath power and denieth the truth, shall be denied the kingdom of God and be trodden down into hell, whence he cometh not forth again. How are we frail and deceitful, workers of sin! We do not repent daily, but daily do we commit sin upon sin.

1.label: Fragment 3
1.text: That ye may know this, dearly beloved brethren, that our works ⟨are judged, hearken to that which⟩ is written in this book: ‘it shall be for a memorial against us in the day of judgement.’ There shall be neither witnesses nor companions; neither shall judgement be given by gifts; for there is nothing better than faith, truth, chastity, fasting, and almsgiving which putteth out all sins. And that which thou wouldest not have done to thyself, do not unto another.

1.label: Fragment 4
1.text: Agree thou for the kingdom of God and thou shalt receive the crown which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
